capabilities.name: Problem Framing Canvas
capabilities.purpose: Guide a structured Look Inward / Look Outward / Reframe process (MITRE Problem Framing Canvas) to produce a bias-checked problem statement and How-Might-We question before any solution is discussed.
inputs: who is believed to experience it, if known
the solution people are already anchored on, if any
outputs: problem statement (Look Inward + Look Outward findings)
selection_cues: a solution is being proposed before the problem is established
team may be solving the wrong problem or missing overlooked stakeholders
anti_cues: problem is already well-understood and validated
tactical bug fix or technical debt with no framing ambiguity
stakeholders already committed to a solution (address alignment first)
context_requirements: any existing problem statement or stakeholder request
evaluation_signals: problem statement is falsifiable and specific (who/what/when/consequence/root cause)
avoids naming a solution as the problem
surfaces who benefits from the status quo

capabilities.name: Discovery Question Set
capabilities.purpose: Ask a small set of targeted context questions to identify the dominant uncertainty and the cheapest way to learn about it, rather than guessing a framework.
selection_cues: it is unclear who or what should be studied
multiple plausible next steps exist and the right one is not obvious
anti_cues: the dominant uncertainty is already known
the decision is purely about UX/interaction, not user/need evidence
a full discovery cycle is clearly warranted (use discovery-process instead)
capabilities.composability: feeds Research Agent delegation or prioritization-comparison; escalates to discovery-process if the uncertainty turns out to need a full cycle
evaluation_signals: identifies one dominant uncertainty rather than a list of everything unknown

capabilities.name: Discovery Process
capabilities.purpose: Run a complete discovery cycle from problem hypothesis to validated solution, orchestrating problem framing, customer interviews, synthesis, and experimentation into one structured process.
inputs: starting problem hypothesis, even a rough one
prior research, customer access, timeline, and the decision discovery must inform, if known
selection_cues: a full discovery cycle is warranted, not just a targeted question
setting up continuous discovery as an ongoing practice
anti_cues: the dominant uncertainty is narrow enough for discovery-question-set alone
no time/access for interviews or experiments — use the lighter capability instead
context_requirements: the decision this discovery must inform
capabilities.composability: typically follows problem-framing-canvas; feeds prioritization-advisor or prd-development
evaluation_signals: confirms or invalidates the hypothesis with evidence, not opinion
avoids 'build it and they will come' without validation

capabilities.name: Prioritization Comparison
capabilities.purpose: Compare credible alternatives (including do-nothing) on value, risk, confidence, effort, and opportunity cost to support a prioritization recommendation.
outputs: opportunity cost of the top choice
selection_cues: multiple credible options exist and it is unclear what to do first
HH asks what should be prioritized
anti_cues: the problem itself is not yet established
the team hasn't yet picked a scoring framework (use prioritization-advisor first)
capabilities.composability: consumes problem-framing-canvas / discovery-question-set output; often follows prioritization-advisor; feeds prd-readiness-gate

capabilities.name: Prioritization Advisor
capabilities.purpose: Ask adaptive questions about product stage, team context, and stakeholder dynamics to recommend which prioritization framework (RICE, ICE, value/effort, etc.) fits the situation, avoiding framework whiplash or a mismatched framework.
inputs: what is being prioritized and why now
product stage, team size, data availability, if known
selection_cues: team keeps arguing about how to prioritize, not just what to prioritize
unsure whether RICE/ICE/value-effort/other fits this team/stage
anti_cues: a framework is already agreed and just needs to be applied (use prioritization-comparison)
only one option exists — no prioritization decision to make
capabilities.composability: typically precedes prioritization-comparison (advisor picks the framework, comparison applies it)
evaluation_signals: avoids recommending a strategic-bet framework like RICE for data-poor early-stage decisions or vice versa
gives a framework matched to actual stated context, not a default favorite

capabilities.name: PRD Readiness Gate
capabilities.purpose: Check whether a decision is sufficiently mature (problem clear, direction selected, acceptance criteria actionable) before allowing transition to a formal PRD or Engineering delegation.
outputs: list of blocking gaps if not ready
selection_cues: HH or PDM is about to write a PRD or delegate to Engineering
there is doubt about whether discovery is actually finished
anti_cues: no candidate direction has been selected yet
capabilities.composability: gate before prd-development; typically the last step before Engineering delegation if no full PRD is needed
evaluation_signals: does not block once criteria are genuinely met

capabilities.name: PRD Development
capabilities.purpose: Orchestrate problem framing, user research synthesis, solution definition, and success criteria into a structured, engineering-ready PRD.
inputs: feature or initiative the PRD covers
discovery notes, problem statements, user research, success metrics, constraints, if available
outputs: structured PRD (problem, users, solution, success criteria)
selection_cues: prd-readiness-gate has passed and the actual PRD document needs to be written
moving from scattered discovery notes to an engineering-ready spec
anti_cues: discovery is not yet mature (run prd-readiness-gate first)
only a lightweight requirements note is needed, not a full PRD
context_requirements: discovery notes / problem statement / success metrics
capabilities.composability: follows prd-readiness-gate; typically the last PDM-owned step before Engineering delegation
evaluation_signals: connects problem, users, solution, and success criteria coherently
avoids the 'build what's in my head' trap by making assumptions explicit
